shared_elements: carved stone slab/monolith surface in low relief
horizontal band or register line dividing an upper zone from the rest
row of repeated figures arranged side by side along the top
band of small repeated vertical marks (row of ticks/signs)
justification: Both are tall sandstone-coloured carved slabs whose upper zone holds a row of side-by-side figures cut off from the lower field by a horizontal band above a strip of small repeated vertical marks, and both include profile animals/birds and disc motifs. But A is a shallow, precisely incised, densely text-filled rounded-top stela with regimented horizontal lines, while B is a boldly modelled, sculpturally rounded high-relief pillar with a few large, sparsely placed creatures and no ordered rows, so the manner of cutting and overall density are wholly unlike.
